lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Leafs beat the Islanders 4-2, moving to 9-14 on the season. They sit 12th in eastern conference, and the standings race sharpens a little every night. Before that, the club lost to the Blue Jackets 3-4. There is runway left in the schedule, and the work on rotations and matchups matters as much as the scoreboard. Next up: at Bruins on Fri 11/27 at 1:00 PM ET. The NHL calendar has flipped to building season - draft prep, trade talks, and the roster surgery that shapes the next contending window. For the Toronto Maple Leafs, the work runs from the draft table to the trade market, and the choices made this summer will define the next window.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season is over, and Toronto has finally put a serious marker down for the next one. The Blue Jays agreed to a five-year, $80-million contract with Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira - a $5-million signing bonus included, with an opt-out after 2029 - giving a club that finished with minus-2.0 points a needed jolt of conviction. Taira is expected to get a chance to start, but this cannot be the last big swing. His arrival may cool the pursuit of Adrian Morejon, yet it sharpens the question of whether Toronto can add the bat this roster still needs. Seiya Suzuki remains the obvious target, and landing him would give the Jays three Japanese stars alongside Taira and Kazuma Okamoto. Watch the next move: whether Toronto turns one headline signing into a coherent roster overhaul before camp opens March 25 at Yankee Stadium.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The floor keeps dropping out from under Toronto - and Monday's loss made the crater deeper. The Raptors fell 116-111 to Milwaukee, handing a 6-11 opponent its first win in 13 games. That makes Toronto 6-11, fourth in the Atlantic and 7.5 games behind, with a one-game losing streak and a -2.5 point differential that tells the story of a team losing close enough to frustrate and often enough to matter. Kawhi Leonard remains the central absence: he has begun individual on-court work, but the knee swelling will keep him out at least another week. The Raptors have gone 6-11 without him, and the offense has lacked the late-game authority a veteran star supplies. Friday's 7:30 p.m. meeting with Brooklyn is no rescue mission - it is a test of whether Toronto can stop the slide before Leonard's return becomes the season's only plan.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The season's pulse returned Monday night, and Washington now has something better than hope: evidence. The Commanders beat Cincinnati 22-20, their second straight victory, as a defense that once looked lost in translation finally began speaking the same language. That makes Washington 4-5-1, second in the NFC East and two games behind - alive, but hardly entitled to optimism. The defense held Joe Burrow's Bengals below their usual standard, a meaningful sign for a club built on learning a new system rather than pretending it had mastered one. Now Brandon Aiyuk arrives for a visit after going unclaimed on waivers, a potentially important jolt for an offense that needs more answers. No injury update changes the central task: keep stacking wins. Next comes Sunday's 4:25 p.m. visit to Arizona, where the Commanders must prove this two-game streak is a turn, not a tease.

article.title: Blue Jays Sign Kaima Taira to Five-Year Deal
paragraphs: The Blue Jays have agreed to sign Japanese right-hander Kaima Taira to a five-year, $80-million contract, sources told multiple outlets. The deal reportedly includes a $5-million signing bonus and an opt-out after the third season. Toronto opens next season at the Yankees on March 25 at 1:35 p.m. ET.

The Leafs, 9-14, visit Boston on Friday at 1 p.m. ET on TSN, with William Nylander's uneven start drawing attention. The Raptors, 6-11, host the Nets Friday at 7:30 p.m. ET, while Kawhi Leonard is out at least another week with a knee ailment. The Commanders are 4-5-1 before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET visit to Arizona on Fox, and Brandon Aiyuk is scheduled to visit Washington.
